Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service San Diego CA
1255 PM PST Fri Nov 20 2026

..SYNOPSIS...
Cooler weather remains across the region through early next week. A 
weak weather system will bring a slight chance of light showers 
closer for parts of Southern California on Sunday night into Monday 
morning. Cooler and drier weather will continue for Tuesday before 
another weather system nears the region, which may bring a chance 
for light showers closer to the coast sometime around Wednesday into 
the early part of Thanksgiving Day. High pressure will move into the 
region later next week, bringing drier and warmer weather. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...FOR EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA INCLUDING ORANGE...
SAN DIEGO...WESTERN RIVERSIDE AND SOUTHWESTERN SAN BERNARDINO 
COUNTIES...

The area of low pressure that impacted the region yesterday will 
continue to move eastward, bringing drier weather through the 
afternoon with decreasing clouds expected from the coast to the 
foothills into the evening. Relatively zonal/weakly offshore flow 
takes over for the weekend, with temperatures remaining 5 to 10 
degrees below normal for areas away from the coast. This will 
include some chilly mornings across parts of the Inland Empire 
lowering into the 30s, high desert regions dipping below freezing, 
and areas around Big Bear Lake dropping into the teens. Winds will 
be breeziest along the coastal slopes tonight out of the north and 
east with gusts mainly below 35 MPH.

A stronger low pressure system is expected to churn off the Pacific 
Northwest coastline over the weekend. A shortwave will break away, 
pushing over SoCal by Sunday into early Monday. There has been a 
slight uptick in trends regarding precipitation amounts with this 
system; an increase in PWAT is also noted, though the atmosphere 
still looks to be on the drier side. Chances for light precipitation 
are now in the forecast from Sunday evening/night for all areas 
except the lower deserts; some showers may linger into southern San 
Diego County (including the metro area) into Monday morning. The 
rain will be light, with general amounts near one tenth of inch, 
locally higher in the mountains. Snow levels will be near 5,000 
feet, with communities in the San Bernardino Mts having the best 
chance to see accumulating snowfall. Snow amounts look to be 
generally under one inch for places like Big Bear Lake.

Models are in fair agreement regarding another area of low pressure 
moving closer to the Pacific Northwest by early next week. There 
still remains some uncertainty in model guidance if a shortwave 
breaks off from the system, similar to what the Sunday/Monday system 
will do...or if the ridge to our south keeps the system north of our 
region. If the system is able to move over our area, we will see a 
chance for light showers sometime Wednesday into Thursday morning 
closer to the coast. Otherwise, dry weather will continue for many 
by the middle and end of next week as the ridge from the south 
amplifies. This will bring a warming trend with highs 5 to 10 
degrees above normal.

&&

.AVIATION... 
201800Z...SCT-BKN clouds around 3500-5000 feet MSL prevails across 
coastal San Diego County today with VFR conditions expected across 
the board. A stray shower is possible along the coastal areas into 
the early afternoon, but there is less than a 5% chance. Westerly 
winds gusting 25-30 kts through mountain gaps into adjacent deserts 
through 23Z.

&&

.MARINE...
Winds and seas remain elevated in the outer waters into this 
evening. Wind gusts 25-30 kts are expected with choppy, locally 
steep, seas of 6-8 feet. A Small Craft Advisory remains in effect 
until 9 PM this evening for the outer waters and contains more 
details. No additional marine hazards are expected thereafter 
through Tuesday.

The next storm system and associated swell is forecast to move into 
the region for Wednesday into Thursday, which could increase wind 
and wave heights back to hazardous levels. There remains uncertainty 
in the forecast track/strength of this storm, so stay tuned for 
details in the coming days.

&&

.BEACHES...
Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 
feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, with 
the King Tides peaking on Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning 
on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet. Background surf 
on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, 
but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably 
higher surf beginning on Thursday. A Coastal Flood Advisory has been 
issued for Sunday morning through Tuesday morning for the rising 
high tides, with a Coastal Flood Watch in effect for Tuesday morning 
through Thursday afternoon.

NOTE: Forecast tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical 
predictions accordingly, based on trends in recent observations.

&&

.SKYWARN... 
Skywarn activation is not requested. However weather spotters are
encouraged to report significant weather conditions.

&&

.SGX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
CA...Coastal Flood Advisory from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday for 
     Orange County Coastal Areas-San Diego County Coastal Areas.

     Coastal Flood Watch from late Monday night through Thursday 
     afternoon for Orange County Coastal Areas-San Diego County 
     Coastal Areas.

PZ...Small Craft Advisory until 9 PM PST this evening for Waters from 
     San Mateo Point to the Mexican Border Extending 10 to 60 nm 
     out including San Clemente Island.
